_status: Reconciled against the canonical commercial contract under an explicit owner decision (2026-09-19).
_authority: config/commercial-contract.json is canonical. These INR (paise) values are what workers/intel-gateway charges via Razorpay, and they must equal that contract's inr_monthly/inr_annual x 100 for every tier. scripts/verify_commercial_contract.py fails the build on drift.
_note: PRO and ENTERPRISE paise values are UNCHANGED and remain exactly what Razorpay charges today (confirmed live). ENTERPRISE annual needed no change at all: INR 416,000 already equals $4,990 at this platform's own rate (INR 41,600 / $499 = 83.3667 INR/USD), so the previously published '$4,790/yr' was a mis-stated USD display of a correct INR charge, not a wrong charge -- the owner's $4,990 decision confirms the live figure.
_mssp_change: MSSP IS A REAL BILLING CHANGE, not a display fix. Monthly moves 16660000 -> 8330000 paise (INR 166,600 -> INR 83,300) and annual 166600000 -> 83300000 paise (INR 1,666,000 -> INR 833,000). Reason: the owner decided on 2026-09-19 that MSSP is $999/month, resolving the production contradiction in which Labs charged $999/mo for MSSP while this gateway charged INR 166,600/mo (= $1,999/mo at the rate above) -- the two platforms were charging different amounts for the same tier. The INR figures here are DERIVED from that USD decision at the platform rate ($999 x 83.3667 = INR 83,283, rounded to INR 83,300 to match the whole-hundred convention of the PRO/ENTERPRISE rows); the owner supplied USD, not INR. Confirm this INR figure, and check for active MSSP subscriptions still billing at the old amount, before releasing.
_usd: usd_monthly/usd_annual are the contract USD list prices for display (Cyber Watchdog offer, /api/pricing). Razorpay charges the paise fields only. Both must equal config/commercial-contract.json; scripts/verify_commercial_contract.py fails the build on drift.
